key_insight: LCA is a model-agnostic orchestration framework that separates oncology data routing from AI inference to make clinical decision support more modular and scalable.
clinical_relevance: It could help hospitals integrate multimodal cancer data and swap AI models more safely without redesigning the whole system.
method: Defines LCA as a 7-tuple architecture with strict separation between orchestration and model logic
Uses an Entry Theory based on Geometric Deep Learning to standardize multimodal patient data
Routes data through a Cancer Switching Module and outputs a Standardized Intermediate Payload (SIP)
evidence_signal: A proof-of-concept tested four technical scenarios and reported negligible overhead, invariant routing during model swaps, and 100% recall for targeted supplementary data requests under injected anomalies.
watch_item: The framework was evaluated as a technical proof-of-concept, so real-world performance, interoperability, and workflow integration still need clinical validation.
paper_title: The Large Cancer Assistant (LCA): A Model-Agnostic Orchestration Framework for Scalable Clinical Decision Support in Oncology
